headline: DeFi narrative remains strong; RV has been a particularly strong mover as institutions can understand yield-bearing tokens that act like a bank
reasoning: Shew highlights RV as a strong recent mover within DeFi. He argues the DeFi narrative is durable because large institutions can understand it — it operates similarly to a bank, paying interest on held tokens. This institutional comprehensibility is seen as a key driver for continued inflows and price appreciation.
quote: Some of the main altcoins RV has definitely been a really strong mover as of late. The defy narrative is not going to go away because the large institutions can understand it. It acts quite similar to a bank with interests being paid on tokens being held. So that's a that's a big driver.

headline: Bullish on crypto broadly: macro tailwinds from easing inflation and falling rates create a positive environment for high-risk assets, with Bitcoin ETF inflows hitting $2.4bn in one week — the largest since October 2025
reasoning: Joe Shew argues that the Clarity Act failing to pass is a bump in the road rather than a permanent setback, and the SEC is still approving positive crypto measures such as tokenized trading. More importantly, the macro environment of easing inflation and falling interest rates creates a constructive backdrop for high-risk assets like crypto. Bitcoin ETF inflows of $2.4bn in one week — the largest since October 2025 — underscore strong institutional demand.
quote: The big drivers aren't just things like clarity act. And I think too many people get caught up on a singular thing that if this happens, then this will change all these other things where big things like the macro environment easing and inflation easing and therefore interest rates can be pushed further down the track. That creates a positive environment for high risk assets like crypto. And this is part of the reason that we saw Bitcoin move so strongly recently. But the inflows for ETFs for Bitcoin in particular have been absolutely massive. We recently saw 2.4 billion inflows in one week, which is the largest week we've seen since October 2025, which was obviously a very strong period back then.

headline: Privacy token worth watching as public concern about personal data harvesting grows, making privacy a major secular tailwind
reasoning: Shew highlights Zcash (ZEC) as a strong and noteworthy mover driven by the growing privacy narrative. He argues that beyond crypto-native privacy concerns, broader societal concern about data harvesting is driving demand for privacy solutions across data, money, and identity. Zcash, as a leading privacy token, is well positioned to benefit from this trend.
quote: As has Zcash. Um, ZC is the ticker for that. And that's because it's a privacy token. And privacy is massive for crypto investors in particular. But now I think because of how, um, people's data is being farmed from them, people are wanting more privacy around everything their data, their money, um, their identity. And cryptos like Zcash offer that. So that's definitely a strong one that's worth watching as well.

headline: Strong mover on AI agent narrative; positioning itself as the platform for AI agent transactions
reasoning: Shew flags Near (NEAR) as a strong mover driven by the AI agent narrative. Near is attempting to brand itself as the platform of choice for AI agents and the transactions they conduct. Given the massive attention on AI as a thematic, this has provided a significant positive price catalyst.
quote: Near near price calls. A very strong mover because of AI agents. So Nia's trying to name themselves the platform for AI agents and the transactions that they do. And AI is obviously a massive narrative. So that's had a really positive move as of late.

headline: Four-year cycle is trending similarly but behaving differently due to institutional money: market has moved out of the bottoming/price-low-discovery phase into a bullish, constructive environment earlier than expected
reasoning: Shew notes that the classic four-year crypto cycle patterns are visible but the market is behaving differently this time due to institutional capital flows. The market cap is still small enough that large institutional inflows can move it rapidly. Notably, Bitcoin hit an all-time high before the halving — something never seen before — suggesting the cycle has shifted earlier. He believes the market has now left the bottoming phase and entered a more positive, bullish phase.
quote: I think the four year cycles, everyone's trying to overlay these on charts. They see it all the time. It makes me laugh. So I think that we see the patterns and we see the consistency, and that's a really positive thing to watch and note this time we have moved earlier before the Bitcoin halving. When that was last year or the year before, we saw the strong move in price and happened before that as well. We saw an all time high come into play before the bitcoin halving. We'd never seen that before either. So I think that whilst the market is behaving in the same way, it's also very different because of the institutional drive. So when the money comes into the market, because the market cap is still very small, it can change very quickly. So we are everyone was waiting until October the 5th. That was the date at the bottom of the cycle. Yet here we are, clearly not at the bottom of the cycle with a few days to go.
